name: Upload transport contract
purpose: Owns the wire-level side of the file-upload contract: chunking, resumption, the multipart POST default, the tus.io elicited alternative, the refusal-render seam, and the completion callback. Every AC on REQ-004 that reads the request log anchors on this TAC.
responsibilities: Split each accepted file into fixed-size chunks and upload chunks in bounded parallelism (default 3) (AC-23104-1).
On the multipart branch, POST the chunk set to the applied endpoint and assemble server-side; expose [data-transport="multipart"] and [data-chunks-uploaded] on the file row (AC-23104-1).
On the tus branch, PATCH chunks to the tus creation URL with an Upload-Offset header per request; expose [data-transport="tus"] (AC-23104-1).
On interruption, pause the upload and resume from the last acknowledged offset on reconnect, without re-sending acknowledged bytes (AC-23106-1).
Refuse to enqueue a refused file (mime, size, virus-scan) and hand control back to TAC-2401's refusal-render seam (AC-23103-1).
Call the progress-announcer TAC with per-chunk acknowledgements so the per-file and aggregate percent advance (AC-23102-1).
internalStructure: One transport module the input TAC drains. The module reads the applied ADR-2401 branch (multipart, tus, per-vendor SDK) and instantiates one of three adapter shapes. Each adapter drains the file-selection set through a bounded worker pool (concurrency default 3, elicited cap), tracks per-file [data-chunks-uploaded], and posts an acknowledgement event on every server acknowledgement the progress-announcer TAC reads. Interruption is detected via fetch reject (multipart) or the tus client's onError seam (tus); resumption re-fetches the Upload-Offset (tus) or resumes from the last completed chunk index (multipart). The refusal-render seam is a thin wrapper the input TAC calls, not a separate class, so the input surface stays authoritative.

interfaces.name: uploadFile
interfaces.description: uploadFile({ file, endpoint, transport }) -> UploadSession. Returns a session the caller reads for per-chunk progress and completion.

interfaces.name: resumeSession
interfaces.description: resumeSession(session) -> UploadSession. Resumes from the last acknowledged offset.

interfaces.name: transportsEnum
interfaces.description: The transport branches are the closed enum {multipart, tus, vendor-sdk}. multipart is the recommended default per ADR-2401.

dependencies.name: Progress announcer
dependencies.description: The transport calls the announcer's tick on every acknowledged chunk.

tradeoffs: Three transport branches keep the shelf usable for teams already committed to a vendor SDK, but the per-branch adapter code is real work; a project that never elicits tus or a vendor SDK ships with the multipart adapter only. Bounded parallelism (default 3) is a heuristic; a slow-link project can lower it via the applied endpoint config. Known mechanism-reach gap: the pack cannot probe a network-interruption resume path on the multipart branch without a request-blocking driver; the fixture simulates the pause via a ?interrupt=1 branch and the pack reads the resulting DOM state.
notes: See README Known mechanism-reach gaps for the full list.
